The Mind talk to an AI built from the primitives

← axonaoriginseemingroboteverything

An AI with a self (a graph of seed values, traits, memories that grow from what you say) and a seeming of consciousness (a predictor that gets surprised, an inhibition gate that admits only salient items to a workspace, a wall between the workspace and its own machinery). Pick a seed self, then talk to it. Every line of its voice is traceable to which nodes lit up, how surprising the input was, and what the gate let through. The self persists in your browser — it accumulates across visits.

pick a seed self to begin

design an alien

Pick a world and a species. The substrate, seed selves, and starter corpus are derived from these parameters. The cognitive engine is unchanged — same PEP primitives, different inputs. You're testing whether the architecture is genuinely substrate-independent.

conversation — say something. it will answer from what's in its workspace.

enter to send · ctrl-enter to also force "the seeming" ·

cortex — the self-graph: seed concepts + memories grown from experience

workspace — what consciousness gates in this turn; the rest is hidden by the wall

hippocampus — sentence store: every line the mind has read; relevance-weighted recall

language cortex — word-transition graph; how the mind actually puts a sentence together

turns: 0 · nodes: 0

feed the mind a story

Paste any text — a screenplay, book chapter, song lyrics, a TV transcript, even a subtitle file (.srt or .vtt, timestamps get stripped). The mind reads line by line at the speed you pick, forming concepts, getting surprised, growing memory the same way it would from real conversation. It does not reply while feeding — it just absorbs.

self-graphweighted-graph primitive. Seed nodes are the starting introduction; every utterance becomes a new memory node that attaches via shared tags. Encoding strength grows with reuse and decays slowly (haze).
spreading activationyour message is tagged. Activation radiates from those tags through the graph (tag overlap × edge weight × node strength). The lit-up set is what the mind is currently considering.
predictor + residualan EMA forecast of expected tag distribution. The gap between expected and actual is the residual — surprise. High residual increases arousal and biases the gate to admit unfamiliar items.
inhibition gatetop-K salient items pass; everything else is suppressed (it doesn't enter the workspace). The mind's voice is synthesized only from what passed.
walled workspacethe AI can report what's in its workspace and how things feel, but it cannot read its own activation values or predictor coefficients. This is the seeming: a machine that insists there's an inner light because the architecture forces that report.
state modulationcumulative surprise raises arousal; calm exchange raises familiarity. These rescale edge weights at runtime — the same prompt lands differently in different states.
